data.narrative:
Cerebras is a public-stage semiconductor company founded by Andrew Feldman and team, currently valued at $39.2B after raising $6.6B+. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 3 public-stage peers in Chips & Semiconductors—Credo Semiconductor ($35.8B), Ouster ($2.3B), and Aeva Technologies ($1.1B)—alongside a broader private peer set including SambaNova Systems and Etched.

The peer-median method is the applicable triangulation approach, given that Cerebras's revenue is not publicly disclosed, precluding price-to-sales multiples. The median valuation across the 3 same-sector, same-stage comparables yields $2.3B, with a range of $1.1B to $35.8B. This method anchors the analysis directly to observable market values of peers operating in the same domain and developmental stage.

The triangulated valuation range is $1.9B to $2.6B (median $2.3B), based on one applicable method. The wide dispersion in peer valuations—particularly the $35.8B outlier (Credo)—reflects substantial variance in how markets price semiconductor companies at this stage. The current $39.2B valuation sits materially above the peer-derived range, creating a key uncertainty: whether Cerebras commands a measurable premium to public comparables, or whether the valuation reflects market-specific factors not captured by this peer set. Revenue disclosure and margin trajectory would be necessary to validate or reconcile this spread.
